movesets.name: Boots Pivot
movesets.description:
Meowscarada is one of the tier's premier offensive pivots thanks to its stupendous Speed, a critical benchmark that lets it outspeed scary threats like Cinderace, Iron Valiant, and Serperior. Knock Off scares some of the tier's key dangers like Deoxys-S, Dragapult, and Gholdengo while simultaneously threatening to cripple other switch-ins like Hatterene and Corviknight. Flower Trick cuts through bulky threats such as Dondozo, Great Tusk, and Primarina, even ignoring the former two's potential Defense boosts, while Triple Axel gives Meowscarada a crucial Ice-type STAB move that allows it to nail common Pokemon such as Clodsire, Gliscor, and Raging Bolt. U-turn keeps up momentum while chipping switch-ins such as Kingambit and Hatterene. Heavy-Duty Boots is practically a requirement on this set, as Meowscarada will frequently be switching in and out of combat and is otherwise quite weak to hazards. Tera Grass and Dark enhance Flower Trick and Knock Off, while Tera Fire is an option that grants Meowscarada some crucial resistances to Fairy, Ice, and Steel-type attacks such as those from Enamorus, Darkrai, and Choice Scarf Gholdengo. Tera Electric is an additional option that allows Meowscarada to feast on Zapdos more effectively thanks to a newly gained Static immunity and resistance to both of its STAB moves.

Meowscarada fits best on balance teams that need a way to force hazard chip along with Knock Off spam to whittle down or outright threaten Pokemon that otherwise don't mind Knock Off such as Gliscor. Meowscarada's frailty courtesy of its pitiful bulk is sometimes hard to work around and limits its switch in opportunities, especially with common weaknesses courtesy of its exploitable defensive typing and a nasty 4x weakness to U-turn. Furthermore, Meowscarada, while being quite fast, is still outsped by monsters such as Darkrai, Dragapult, Weavile, and Zamazenta, the latter of which happens to be one of Meowscarada's best checks. Weavile's offensive tenacity combined with deadly Speed makes it a potent threat, which is why Rocky Helmet Skarmory is one of Meowscarada's best partner options on balance teams, as it punishes Triple Axel spam and shrugs off Weavile's hits comparatively easily. Meowscarada's role as an offensive pivot helps chip away at opposing cores while also bringing some of their key defensive threats into OHKO range for some frail teammates like Darkrai, Iron Boulder, and Gholdengo. Dragapult is another great partner for Meowscarada; it can blank Fighting-type attacks and follow up with a fast Will-O-Wisp to neuter Zamazenta as well. Meowscarada's defensive woes can be covered by bulky teammates that don't mind taking coverage moves from faster threats. On the physical side, Great Tusk's role as a physically bulky offensive spinner with synergistic typing opens up multiple opportunities to clear hazards. On the special side, Clodsire and Galarian Slowking are both impressive partners thanks to their longevity and fantastic defensive profiles, with the former being able to blank setup sweepers like Darkrai and the latter being able to continue Meowscarada's momentum chain by using a slow Chilly Reception to take a hit or scout a switch, allowing Meowscarada to come in safely. Additionally, Galarian Slowking also threatens Pokemon that would commonly switch into Meowscarada like Iron Defense Zamazenta with Future Sight.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
With a Choice Scarf equipped, Meowscarada serves as one of the fastest pivots and revenge killers in the game, matching well against many faster threats such as Dragapult and Deoxys-S as well as many boosted threats such as Speed Booster Energy Iron Valiant and opposing Choice Scarf users like Gholdengo, Landorus-T, and Latios. Knock Off helps remove items such as Heavy-Duty Boots and Rocky Helmet from switch-ins such as Corviknight, Galarian Weezing, and Moltres, allowing Meowscarada to continue chipping them down safely while making it easier to break through long-term. U-turn pivots out of bad matchups like the aforementioned checks, generating progress for Meowscarada’s teammates by helping them get onto the field safely as well as stinging Hisuian Samurott, Darkrai, and Ogerpon-W. Triple Axel hits Gliscor, Landorus-T, Dragonite, and Choice Scarf Enamorus incredibly hard, OHKOing all of them, as well as being Meowscarada’s strongest neutral attack against Iron Valiant and Kyurem, letting it revenge kill them after they are chipped. Flower Trick can be used to revenge kill Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott and Tera Water Ogerpon-W even after a Trailblaze as well as muscle past Dondozo and Garganacl even after a Defense boost. Alternatively, Trick can help Meowscarada cripple walls such as Corviknight and Galarian Weezing, giving it the flexibility of being able to switch moves later in a game, especially against bulkier teams where the extra Speed is not as necessary. It can also cripple Kingambit and other setup sweepers like Zamazenta and Hatterene that Meowscarada can't threaten easily if they're still healthy. Tera Ghost is used for an immunity to Extreme Speed from Dragonite and Fighting-type moves such as Body Press from Zamazenta and Vacuum Wave from Iron Valiant, allowing Meowscarada to potentially flip its matchup and revenge kill or neutralize them in an emergency. However, after Terastallizing, Meowscarada’s attacks do not get a Protean boost, so it should be used carefully.

Choice Scarf Meowscarada sees use on offense and bulky offense teams that appreciate having a fast pivot that can outspeed most forms of traditional speed control. Pokemon such as Ting-Lu, Iron Treads, and Garchomp pair very well with Meowscarada, as they can set entry hazards to build up chip damage over time, while Meowscarada helps remove Heavy-Duty Boots from users such as Zamazenta, Moltres, and Galarian Weezing. Ting-Lu can also switch into special attackers that threaten Meowscarada such as Heatran and Iron Moth. Gholdengo is a natural fit that synergizes perfectly with Meowscarada, helping against many of its checks such as Zamazenta, Kyurem, Galarian Weezing, and Corviknight. Raging Bolt can handle Moltres, Scizor, and Zapdos and form a VoltTurn pivoting core with Meowscarada if it has Volt Switch, while Meowscarada can help against Ground-types such as Ting-Lu and Gliscor that annoy Raging Bolt. Meowscarada’s frailty leaves it vulnerable to priority users that can circumvent its high Speed such as Lokix, Kingambit, and Dragonite. Therefore, Pokemon such as Moltres, Great Tusk, and Corviknight are valued for their ability to deal with these threats; furthermore, Moltres can bring Meowscarada in safely with U-turn, Great Tusk can remove entry hazards to let Meowcarada pivot around more freely, and Corviknight can do both. Additional pivots that complement Meowscarada well include Galarian Slowking and Iron Crown for their ability to check Clefable, Pecharunt, and Galarian Weezing as well as pressure switch-ins to Meowscarada such as Zamazenta with Future Sight. Against bulkier teams, wallbreakers such as Ogerpon-W, Swords Dance Gliscor, and Nasty Plot Tornadus-T are great assets, as they can overwhelm shared checks such as Corviknight and Zapdos and break the balance cores that Meowscarada struggles against. Similarly, other wallbreakers like Zamazenta and Kyurem can help keep up the pressure against these teams.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
Thanks to an excellent Speed tier, Protean, and a great offensive movepool, Choice Band Meowscarada is a solid wallbreaker and pivot that can also act as a decent revenge killer. Meowscarada's STAB moves help in emphasizing its wallbreaking role; the critical hits provided by Flower Trick can break through Defense-boosting threats like Great Tusk, Dondozo, and Garganacl, and Knock Off removing held items like Heavy-Duty Boots and Rocky Helmet from checks like Moltres, Galarian Weezing, and Corviknight makes it easier for Meowscarada to overwhelm them long-term. On top of threatening OHKOs on foes like Ogerpon-W and Rillaboom, Meowscarada's fast U-turn is a great utility move that can get it out of bad matchups as well as do solid chip damage throughout a battle to bulkier checks and foes that it can't immediately knock out like Kingambit, Kyurem, and bulky Cinderace while preserving momentum and bringing its teammates in safely. Triple Axel is important to handle Pokemon like Dragonite, Gliscor, Zapdos, and Raging Bolt while being a strong neutral attack against Corviknight and Galarian Weezing. Tera Grass adds an additional boost to Flower Trick, such as 2HKOing a would-be check in Tinkaton, as well as allowing Meowscarada to survive a Moonblast from Enamorus and a Close Combat from Zamazenta if necessary. Tera Dark gives Knock Off some extra power, such as having good odds to 2HKO Moltres and bulky Cinderace, and it gives Meowscarada a stronger defensive profile against threats like Dragonite and Great Tusk's Ice Spinner in a pinch. Tera Ghost allows Meowscarada to dodge Dragonite's Extreme Speed and Zamazenta's Fighting-type moves. It's important to remember that Terastallizing Meowscarada has a big trade-off, as disabling Protean can make it a less effective wallbreaker throughout the game.

Meowscarada fits well on balanced and bulky offense teams. Galarian Slowking is an example of a solid teammate that can tank hits from Zamazenta and Iron Valiant, spread paralysis as a form of speed control, and pivot to Meowscarada safely with Chilly Reception on switch-ins like Ting-Lu, Gholdengo, and opposing Galarian Slowking while also providing it a defensive boost via Protean Triple Axel. Cinderace is a fast offensive pivot with U-turn that can form a solid core with Meowscarada to chip foes down throughout a game. Meowscarada can take advantage of foes like Alomomola, Primarina, and Gliscor that Cinderace invites in, while Cinderace can handle Steel-types like Corviknight and Kingambit that Meowscarada has a hard time dealing with. Meowscarada's early-game pressure is extremely helpful in setting up late-game cleaners like Kingambit, Dragonite, and Zamazenta to overwhelm weakened teams, especially as it puts pressure on foes that check them like Landorus-T, Alomomola, and Great Tusk. Great Tusk, Iron Treads, Hatterene, and the aforementioned Cinderace can deal with entry hazards that Meowscarada is vulnerable to; the former two can also set their own hazards to build up more chip damage for Meowscarada to capitalize on, especially since it can use Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from foes like Dragonite, Moltres, and Kyurem. Defensive Pokemon, such as Zapdos, Moltres, and Corviknight, are difficult checks for Meowscarada to get past; having solid specially-offensive teammates to pivot to safely with U-turn, like Kyurem and Raging Bolt, to deal with these checks allows Meowscarada more freedom to keep wallbreaking. Gholdengo can help switch in on faster Pokemon that threaten Meowscarada like Iron Valiant and Zamazenta; Meowscarda can help Gholdengo in turn by threatening foes it struggles with like Ting-Lu and Blissey. The aforementioned Zapdos, Moltres, and Corviknight are great partners as well, as they can check Pokemon like Zamazenta, Kingambit, Lokix, and Choice Scarf Enamorus and bring Meowscarada in safely with their pivot moves; additionally, Corviknight provides hazard removal with Defog, while Moltres and Zapdos threaten Skarmory and opposing Corviknight.

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Dark (Choice Band)

Thunder Punch may be considered to immediately OHKO Pelipper and always 2HKO Toxapex, but losing out on Knock Off makes Meowscarada's job of breaking Flying teams a lot harder, as it takes too much damage from Rocky Helmet Skarmory. Similarly, Low Kick deals massive damage to Archaludon and lets Meowscarada OHKO Bisharp, but Knock Off lets Meowscarada wear down opposing defensive cores faster.

Grass

Toxic Spikes can serve as a solid option over Flower Trick to better wear down Dark and Dragon teams. Trick can be ran to cripple switch-ins like Skarmory and Toxapex.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf (Dark)
movesets.description:
Choice Scarf Meowscarada provides incredible speed control for Dark teams, being able to outspeed and handle threats such as Flutter Mane, Tornadus-T, and Greninja for its teammates. Flower Trick lets Meowscarada deal with the likes of Flutter Mane, Ting-Lu, and Primarina comfortably. Knock Off takes care of Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gholdengo, Spectrier, and Latios along with removing held items like Archaludon's and Corviknight's Leftovers and Toxapex's Heavy-Duty Boots. Triple Axel can handle Flying- and Dragon-types such as Landorus, Dragonite, and Roaring Moon. Alternatively, Play Rough can pressure opposing Dark-types such as Darkrai while also handling Fighting-types such as Iron Valiant and Gallade. Finally, U-turn provides Meowscarada a way to keep up momentum while also handling Hoopa-U.

Ting-Lu provides great defensive support for Meowscarada, helping to deal with special threats like Choice Scarf Flutter Mane, Raging Bolt, and Iron Moth. Ting-Lu also can set up entry hazards, wearing down checks such as Archaludon and Hippowdon along with handling Steel- and Poison-types such as Heatran, Toxapex, and Sneasler with Earthquake. Mandibuzz can safely pivot Meowscarada in with U-turn and check physical attackers such as Excadrill, Scizor, and Choice Scarf Dragapult with Foul Play. Choice Specs Greninja complements Meowscarada, dealing with Fire-types and physical walls like Iron Moth, Moltres, and Skarmory with Surf. It can also use coverage like Extrasensory or Sludge Wave to better handle problems like Toxapex and the Ogerpon formes, respectively. Hisuian Samurott and Bisharp provide Sucker Punch speed control, dealing with targets faster than Meowscarada like Dragon Dance Dragapult and Swift Swim Barraskewda. Hisuian Samurott also applies further pressure against teams with Spikes from Ceaseless Edge, while Sacred Sword deals with Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra. Bisharp can use Iron Head to help pressure Fairy-types like Hatterene and Clefable for Meowscarada. Assault Vest Hoopa-U can come in on special threats like Galarian Weezing and Kyurem for Meowscarada and answer them with options such as Focus Blast and Psychic. Nasty Plot Darkrai can help break checks such as Pecharunt and bulky Gholdengo with Dark Pulse and uses Sludge Bomb to handle Iron Valiant. Sableye can blanket wall Fighting-types like Iron Hands and Sneasler for Meowscarada alongside using Encore to trap targets like Clodsire and Blissey into undesirable recovery options.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf (Grass)
movesets.description:
Choice Scarf Meowscarada provides incredible speed control for Grass teams, being able to outspeed and handle threats such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Tornadus-T, and Greninja for its teammates. Flower Trick is Meowscarada's strongest offensive option, dealing with the likes of Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Ting-Lu. Knock Off removes Ghost and Psychic-types like offensive Gholdengo, Spectrier, and Latios while removing held items like Archaludon's Leftovers and Toxapex's Rocky Helmet. Triple Axel can handle Flying- and Dragon-types such as Landorus, Dragonite, and Roaring Moon. Finally U-turn provides Meowscarada a way to keep up momentum while threatening Hoopa-U.

Both Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-C can support Meowscarada by threatening Ice-types like Avalugg, Articuno, and Alolan Ninetales. Ogerpon-H can further support Meowscarada by handling problematic Steel-types such as Skarmory, Scizor, and bulky Gholdengo while absorbing Will-O-Wisp from Galarian Weezing and Sableye. Alternatively, Ogerpon-C can check Fire-types such as Volcarona and Moltres. Amoonguss complements Meowscarada defensively by dealing with Fighting- and Fairy-types like Iron Hands, Iron Valiant, and Choice Scarf Flutter Mane; it also absorbs Toxic Spikes to prevent Meowscarada being worn down and uses Spore to get Meowscarada in safely. Sinistcha can also check Fighting-types like Iron Hands and Sneasler as well as Body Press Skarmory. Sinistcha can also use its high Special Attack to break problematic physical walls such as Archaludon and Galarian Weezing. Brambleghast can provide Rapid Spin support to keep Meowscarada healthy and set Spikes to help wear down would-be checks like Archaludon and Toxapex. Hisuian Lilligant can break through Steel- and Dark-types such as Heatran, Bisharp, and Hydreigon. Hydrapple is not weak to Fire and can use Earth Power to check Fire-types such as Heatran and Volcanion.

movesets.name: Choice Band (Dark)
movesets.description:
Choice Band Meowscarada turns the tables on typical checks of its Choice Scarf set, as it 2HKOes Skarmory and Toxapex with minimal chip damage, allowing it to cut through bulkier Water, Flying, and Ground teams. Knock Off removes annoying items like Rocky Helmet and Heavy-Duty Boots on the aforementioned Skarmory and Toxapex, allowing Meowscarada to freely spam Triple Axel and Flower Trick on Flying and Water teams, which at least 2HKOes any Pokemon on these types. Triple Axel is also able to OHKO all the Ogerpon formes and 2HKO Gouging Fire and Corviknight after Stealth Rock damage. Flower Trick OHKOes Primarina and ignores Reflect, which is helpful in the Fairy matchup. U-turn lets Meowscarada pivot out of checks like Archaludon, Porygon2, and Torkoal to bring in teammates such as Choice Specs Hydreigon and Hoopa-U that remove these threats.

Choice Band Meowscarada gets outsped by Flutter Mane and Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, thus being unable to deal with them. However, the lack of Speed can be remedied by pairing it with teammates like Choice Scarf Hoopa-U and Greninja, which can outspeed and remove these threats. Alternatively, Hoopa-U can use a Trick Room or a Choice Specs set to work with Meowscarada to pressure offensive teams like Fighting and Dragon or further batter down opposing defensive cores, as Hoopa-U is able to OHKO Archaludon, Toxapex, and Skarmory. In return, Meowscarada is able to 2HKO specially defensive Corviknight, which Hoopa-U and Greninja appreciate. Choice Specs Greninja and Hydreigon also fullfill these roles, with Greninja having the perk of being able to outspeed the Ogerpon formes and OHKO Moltres, while Hydreigon OHKOes Archaludon and is a Ground-immune teammate that is vital in the matchup against sand-based Ground teams. Kingambit appreciates Meowscarada removing its checks like Skarmory and in return provides priority in Sucker Punch. Entry hazards from Ting-Lu are appreciated, as Meowscarada needs Stealth Rock chip damage to be able to 2HKO Toxapex and Skarmory; Ting-Lu also functions as a defensive pivot against Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Enamorus. Hisuian Samurott is an alternative, as it is able to stack Spikes more efficiently against the opposing team and provides a Fire resistance that is helpful against Volcarona and Ceruledge. Alolan Muk provides a Fairy neutrality, which lets it come into Flutter Mane and Hatterene with ease, and in return, Meowscarada eviscerates Ground-types like Landorus that cause trouble for Alolan Muk. Sableye provides a Fighting immunity, which is helpful against Zamazenta and gives Meowscarada a switch-in to Body Press Skarmory.

movesets.name: CRITTY CAT
movesets.description:
• With its good Attack, Speed, and access to Flower Trick and Knock Off, Meowscarada is a potent cleaner that is also hard to switch into.

  • Flower Trick: With its guaranteed critical hit, Flower Trick is a dangerous cleaning move once foes resistant to it have been sufficiently chipped.

  • U-turn: If using Protean, U-turn lets Meowscarada be a pivot that does far more damage than most other users, and it helps Choice Scarf Meowscarada get out of some tricky early-game situations such as Serperior leads.

  • Trick: Trick can help Choice-locked sets incapacitate an annoying wall, such as Corviknight or Dondozo, by locking them into a single move. It also has the bonus of Protean letting Meowscarada resist Fighting-type attacks after using it.

  • Triple Axel: Triple Axel may not be the most reliable move out there, but it strikes fear into the heart of Dragonite and offensive Mimikyu, which can both be big offensive issues for Meowscarda.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: Jolly is usually preferred for the Speed tie in mirror matches, but Adamant's extra power can be justified on Choice Scarf Meowscarada, since it still outspeeds boosted Garchomp.

  • Choice Band versus Choice Scarf: Choice Band-boosted Meowscarada hits incredibly hard, and with its naturally high Speed, it can serve as a cleaner and a potential wallbreaker, especially against common Defense-boosting foes such as Bulk Up Annihilape and Tera Fairy Archaludon. With the Speed offered via Choice Scarf, Meowscarada can threaten otherwise faster foes, such as Dragapult and +1 Garchomp, potentially putting more pressure on offensive teams.

  • Protean versus Overgrow: Protean’s type shifting allows Meowscarada to make the most of its colorful movepool, particularly on Choice-locked sets, where the limitation to only changing types once is effectively nullified. If you intend to make use of a Tera type other than Grass or Stellar, Overgrow is worth considering, as it allows Meowscarada more flexibility with its moves by not changing type and removing STAB from Flower Trick or Knock Off.

Other Options

  • Play Rough: Compared to Triple Axel, Play Rough isn't nearly as good at handling Dragon-types besides Hydreigon, but it does stop Terastallized Dragonite, Garchomp, and Baxcalibur from grabbing a Speed boost with Scale Shot.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch is a strong priority attack, but it can be rather risky with a Choice item.

  • Brick Break: Low Kick's superior damage output against Ursaluna-B usually makes it the better Fighting-type coverage move, but with Choice Band, Brick Break still OHKOes Kingambit and breaks Alolan Ninetales's Aurora Veil.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Terastallization overriding Protean means Meowscarada should usually only Terastallize to clean a weakened team late-game.

  • Grass: While Terastallizing does override Protean, Tera Grass Meowscarada can be used to power through teams ill-prepared for it. Dual screens teams in particular are especially vulnerable to the sheer power of Choice Band-boosted Tera Grass Flower Trick.

  • Dark: Tera Dark-boosted Knock Off isn't as reliable at sweeping as Flower Trick, but it can surprise bulky Steel-types such as Scizor and Archaludon, as well as deal incredible damage to bulky Volcarona.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost is a defensive option to stop Dragonite's Extreme Speed from revenge killing Meowscarada.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar's one-time boost per attack can give Meowscarada more flexible cleaning options. If Meowscarada Terastallizes after using Protean, the type it currently is will get the double-Base Power boost, which can lead to unexpectedly powerful coverage moves!

  • Fire: Tera Fire gives Meowscarada a Will-O-Wisp immunity and Fire resistance to combat bulky Volcarona.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 76 HP / 228 Atk / 108 Def / 4 SpD / 92 Speed with Jolly: This bulkier Choice Scarf spread allows Meowscarada to outspeed Jolly Garchomp while avoiding an OHKO from Breloom's Mach Punch and Choice Band Dragonite's Extreme Speed.

Minor Optimizations

  • Neutral Natures and Trick: Make sure to use a neutral nature and a Jolly or Adamant Mint on Meowscarada, so it won't get confused by eating any Berry after using Trick.

movesets.name: Focus Sash
movesets.description:
• With its good Speed and wide movepool, Meowscarada makes for a potent lead.

  • Triple Axel: Triple Axel prevents Meowscarada from getting set-up on by Dragonite, and ruins Garchomp and Hydreigon.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch allows Meowscarada to better handle fast foes such as Dragapult and Choice Scarf Gholdengo.

  • Toxic Spikes: Meowscarada is an excellent offensive choice to lay Toxic Spikes, since it puts immense pressure on Ursaluna-B leads.

  • Low Kick: Low Kick is Meowscarada's only way through Kingambit, with the bonus of dealing immense damage to Tera Normal Ursaluna-B.

  • Protean versus Overgrow: Protean offers the most offensive flexibility. For more supportive sets with Toxic Spikes, Overgrow lets it keep STAB on its attacks after it uses its support moves.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Thanks to its good Speed, Meowscarada makes particularly excellent use of Taunt, though two big targets, Archaludon and Annihilape, will put Meowscarada in immense danger.

  • Play Rough: While Triple Axel deals with most Dragon-types better, Play Rough can be a huge upset against Terastallized Scale Shot users like Dragonite and Garchomp!

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: This Meowscarada has very little use for Terastallization, only using it in late-game situations where it can sweep.

  • Grass: When paired with an Overgrow boost, Tera Grass lets Flower Trick deal a huge amount of damage.

  • Dark: Tera Dark makes Knock Off even more difficult to switch into, especially hitting Volcarona hard.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar is the more flexible option for late-game sweeping. Just remember that moves only get the double BP boost if they match Meowscarada's current typing.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost saves Meowscarada from Normal-type priority, which can flip the match on unsuspecting Dragonite!

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Heavy-Duty Boots and Magic Guard + Life Orb sets are niche options that can fit on bulkier teams that appreciate the longevity of such sets given Meowscarada's propensity to pivot often, though the loss in power is often noticeable such as being unable to 2HKO Pecharunt. Mixed sets with Adaptability + Life Orb and Dark Pulse are a niche option to bait checks such as Corviknight. Spikes and Toxic Spikes can also be considered as options to accrue chip damage or force entry hazard removal by Corviknight. Sucker Punch can be considered on Choice Band sets if a team needs priority to check faster threats such as Deoxys-S and Choice Scarf Gholdengo. Lash Out is a niche option that allows Meowscarada to better threaten Intimidate Corviknight and Skarmory.

Checks and Counters

Corviknight and Skarmory: With their significant bulk and 4x resistance to Grass, Meowscarada can struggle greatly in breaking through these counters alone, particularly Fluffy variants, and so requires support from teammates to weaken or remove these foes.

Faster Threats: Meowscarada's lack of bulk and poor defensive typing means Choice Band sets are vulnerable to most offensive threats that outspeed it such as Chien-Pao, Zamazenta, and Deoxys-S as well as various Choice Scarf users such as Roaring Moon and Azelf. Choice Scarf sets are also vulnerable to priority from the likes of Chien-Pao and Kingambit.

movesets.name: Choice Item
movesets.description:
With its good Attack and great Speed tier, Meowscarada serves as a strong offensive pivot and wallbreaker that is able to exploit and outspeed common defensive and offensive staples such as Great Tusk, Roaring Moon, and Gholdengo. Choice Band enables Meowscarada to secure OHKOs against foes such as Scream Tail, Pecharunt, and Great Tusk as well as pressure checks such as Corviknight. Choice Scarf guarantees Meowscarada is able to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame and threaten other Choice Scarf users such as Roaring Moon, Latios, and Scream Tail. U-turn lets Meowscarada scout switch-ins and accumulate chip damage against checks such as Corviknight. Triple Axel threatens checks such as Mandibuzz and defensive Zapdos while also OHKOing targets like Landorus and Garchomp. Low Kick alternatively allows Meowscarada to hit bulky Steel-types such as Cobalion, Heatran, and Kingambit. Both Triple Axel and Low Kick OHKO Roaring Moon. Trick cripples checks such as Corviknight or setup sweepers such as Fluffy Roaring Moon, Iron Crown, and Kingambit.

Meowscarada can fit on a variety of balanced and more offensive teams that appreciate it as a wallbreaker and value its Speed tier above other dangerous offensive threats. Meowscarada can struggle to get onto the field due to its lack of bulk and so appreciates slow pivots like Corviknight, Swampert, and Pecharunt that can also absorb revenge killing attempts from the likes of Chien-Pao, Deoxys-S, and Zamazenta. Meowscarada can also benefit from the presence of offensive pivots like Cinderace, Moltres, and Azelf that provide it with opportunities against switch-ins like Great Tusk, Manaphy, and Swampert. Meowscarada can struggle with breaking through Corviknight and Skarmory and so pairs well with other strong wallbreakers such as Zamazenta, Chien-Pao, and Ogerpon-W that can pressure and overload them. Similarly, it can benefit from strong hazard setters such as Great Tusk, Landorus, Ting-Lu, and Heatran that can chip and weaken Corviknight and other checks like Iron Hands and Zamazenta. Alternatively, Meowscarada can be paired with other strong wallbreakers such as Choice Specs Gholdengo and that can take advantage of a free switch into Corviknight or Skarmory.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Early round 1 onwards

Price Range: 19-20 points

Overview: Meowscarada is a great versatile pick that is an excellent enabler for a draft's centerpiece or wincons. With Protean, it serves as an excellent wallbreaker, revenge killer, or fast pivot with its great coverage options. It is great at forcing opposing switches, allowing it to maintain momentum with STAB U-turn. However, it's relatively frail and struggles to take hits, so it must be brought in safely.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Revenge Killer: Meowscarada can run a Choice Scarf to outspeed other Choice Scarf users, making it an incredibly powerful revenge killer that can maintain momentum with U-turn.

Fast Pivot: Meowscarada's high Speed allows it to outspeed opposing threats and force them out with its powerful attacks. It can also use STAB U-turn with Protean to do lots of damage to switch-ins and position teammates well. When paired with Choice Band, Meowscarada becomes unwallable in many scenarios, though it becomes prone to being revenge killed.

Lead Entry Hazard Setter: Meowscarada can be used to set Spikes or Toxic Spikes at the start of the game. This set is often paired with Taunt, attacking moves such as Knock Off and U-turn, and a Focus Sash.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Flower Trick, Knock Off, Sucker Punch

Utility Moves: Taunt, Spikes, Toxic Spikes, Substitute, Trick, Brick Break

Coverage: U-turn, Triple Axel, Thunder Punch, Low Kick, Play Rough

Niche Moves

Leaf Storm: Leaf Storm is good against defensive walls that Meowscarada struggles breaking through. It is most often ran on entry hazard setting or support sets, especially against physically bulky hazard removers like Great Tusk.

Leech Seed: Leech Seed can be used along with fast Substitute to chip down some of Meowscarada's incoming checks, allowing it to regain most of its health while weakening the foe. However, simply pivoting to a teammate that can better check these foes is almost always preferred.

Common Items

Choice Scarf: Even though Meowscarada is naturally very fast, Choice Scarf is useful for outspeeding Speed-boosting and even faster Pokemon, making it a great revenge killer.

Choice Band: Choice Band gives Meowscarada great wallbreaking or late-game sweeping potential, especially with its already-strong STAB attacks.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Since Meowscarada likes to pivot in and out frequently, Heavy-Duty Boots is a great item on it, allowing it to avoud entry hazard chip over time.

Niche Items

Focus Sash: Focus Sash is good for lead sets, allowing them to get extra entry hazards up or deal extra damage.

Damage-boosting Items: Other damage-boosting items are useful for providing additional damage output, especially when getting Choice-locked into a single move is unideal. It may be better to run Overgrow instead of Protean on these sets to maintain its STAB types.

Protective Pads: Even though Flower Trick does not make contact, Protective Pads is good against Pokemon with contact-related items and abilities, especially when using Triple Axel. The main downside is not being able to utilize other items, especially Heavy-Duty Boots. They both aim to reduce chip damage, so keep in mind which item is more valuable in a given matchup.

Choice Specs: Meowscarada has a decent special movepool, so Choice Specs can be used in matchups where its strong special STAB moves and coverage are enough to offset its lower Special Attack stat.

Leftovers: Leftovers is good for passive recovery, especially on Substitute + Leech Seed builds.

Tera

Meowscarada does not benefit from Terastallization, since it completely negates Protean. If it is made a Tera Captain regardless, it can utilize Tera Grass and Dark to increase STAB damage or Tera Fire for extra coverage.

Draft Strategy

Meowscarada is a great versatile Pokemon that synergizes very well with another top-tier Pokemon. It provides valuable chip damage, item removal, and pivoting, and it can occasionally clean up teams that were weakened by its teammates.

High-tier Tera Captains: Since Meowscarada isn't reliant on Terastallization to function, it pairs extremely well with many of the top-tier Tera Captains in the metagame, including Raging Bolt, Enamorus, and Salamence. It is great at getting them on the field with U-turn and weakening their checks with its strong coverage.

Special Wallbreakers: Meowscarada can be an excellent physical wallbreaker, but it often struggles breaking physical walls. Having a special wallbreaker that it can pivot to keeps its team in a strong position, and it forces the opponent to choose what form of defensive EVs they want to run on their Pokemon. Some good pairings include Iron Valiant, Terapagos, and Iron Bundle.

Ground-types: Ground-types like Great Tusk and Landorus can help check the Poison-, Steel-, and Fire-types that may otherwise wall Meowscarada. Since it can force many switches, it can easily pivot to them safely.

Checks and Counters

Poison-types: Many Poison-types can check Meowscarada well, especially if they are paired with Rocky Helmet to punish it from using U-turn. Muk and Swalot cannot get their Rocky Helmet removed, and they are often drafted on teams that struggle against Meowscarada.

Other Physically Defensive Walls: Few Pokemon can comfortably take Meowscarada's hits, but physically bulky Pokemon that can resist its attacks are typically most reliable, especially if they force Choice sets to make difficult predictions. Examples include Corviknight, Gouging Fire, and Galarian Weezing.

U-turn: Any faster Pokemon with U-turn can easily force Meowscarada out due to its massive weakness to the move.

Chip Damage: Since Meowscarada uses U-turn a lot, Rocky Helmet and other forms of contact damage such as Rough Skin can quickly chip it down. Damage from entry hazards also adds up quickly, especially if it does not want to run Heavy-Duty Boots.

Priority: Meowscarada struggles to take priority attacks, especially after being chipped from entry hazards or contact damage. Vacuum Wave and Mach Punch are very threatening, and moves like Bullet Punch and Extreme Speed can also do massive damage.

movesets.name: Offensive Pivot (Atk)
movesets.description:
Meowscarada is a powerful offensive pivot, utilizing a combination of Protean and high-powered attacks to thrive in the metagame. With an Attack donation, Meowscarada gains a much-needed power boost alongside its naturally high Speed, allowing it to hit hard and fast. Move-wise, Flower Trick and Knock Off are Meowscarada's most spammable moves, while Triple Axel nails would-be switch-ins such as Landorus-T and Mandibuzz. U-turn allows Meowscarada to create momentum to exploit the offensive pressure it is able to apply. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Meowscarada to pivot in multiple times throughout the game, while Choice Band boosts Meowscarada's power to higher levels, and Choice Scarf improves Meowscarada's speed control potential. Tera Grass is chosen to amplify Flower Trick to even higher levels, although Tera Dark is still a viable option to boost Knock Off.

High Attack gods like Calyrex-I and Groudon are excellent for Meowscarada to inherit from. Furthermore, Calyrex-I and Groudon both appreciate Meowscarada's ability to break bulky Water-types such as Rotom-W, while Groudon also breaks Steel-types such as Heatran in turn. However, other Gods such as Zacian-C and Ho-Oh are acceptable alternatives, as they grant small but still noticeable Attack increases. Though Meowscarada functions as a powerful offensive pivot, it is quite frail, thus making defensive pivots such as Rotom-W, Landorus-T, and Pecharunt highly appreciated to allow Meowscarada to enter the field. Meowscarada also appreciates special attackers such as Iron Moth, Hisuian Electrode, and Landorus to break opposing physical walls such as Skarmory, Moltres, and Clefable as well as Pokemon walling all of its coverage like Zacian-C, with the former two also forming a VoltTurn core with Meowscarada. Lastly, Stealth Rock and Spikes users such as Skarmory and Ting-Lu are advantageous, as Meowscarada is able to remove foes' Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off and accumulate chip damage through entry hazards and U-turn.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
• Flower Trick demolishes Water-types such as Primarina, Urshifu-R, and Manaphy.
  • Knock Off crushes Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Cresselia, Espathra, and Skeledirge.
  • Triple Axel hits Dragon-types like Raging Bolt, Flying-types such as Zapdos and both Landorus formes, and Grass-types like opposing Meowscarada and Whimsicott super effectively.
  • Meowscarada's last moveslot is pretty flexible; Giga Impact is its overall strongest pick, taking down foes such as non-Choice Scarf Porygon-Z and low-invested Ogerpon-W and Walking Wake; Play Rough deals with Fighting-types like Urshifu-S and Annihilape and is a better move against some Dragon-types, notably Walking Wake and Kyurem; Thunder Punch is a great option for Corviknight, against which Meowscarada would otherwise have a hard time; Low Kick hits Hisuian Goodra and Kyurem for more damage.
  • A Jolly nature ensures Meowscarada outspeeds Greninja, Serperior, Ogerpon-W, and non-Speed Booster Energy Iron Valiant, while an Adamant nature provides some additional firepower to this set, allowing feats such as OHKOing Custap Berry Skeledirge and most Metagross variants with Knock Off, Porygon-Z with Triple Axel, and Annihilape with Play Rough.
  • Meowscarada struggles against faster Pokemon like Speed Energy Booster Iron Valiant and Choice Scarf users such as Hoopa-U, so it appreciates partners that can deal with them like Hisuian Goodra, Pecharunt, and Corviknight.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf
movesets.description:
Choice Scarf Meowscarada serves as the fastest viable Choice Scarf user in the format, able to revenge kill Pokemon like Dragon Dance Dragonite, Scale Shot Garchomp, and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele. Flower Trick is very useful against Iron Defense Zamazenta as well as Landorus-T attempting to weaken it Meowscarada with Intimidate. Knock Off's fast item removal can support Meowscarada's team by removing crucial items like Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers from Pokemon like Kyurem, Hatterene, and Moltres. U-turn allows Meowscarada to pivot out of bad matchups like Ferrothorn, Heatran, and Moltres, and Triple Axel covers Flying- and Dragon-type Pokemon like Zapdos, Dragonite, and Raging Bolt that aren't threatened by Meowscarada's main attacking options. Protean lets squeeze out extra power from Triple Axel and U-turn via STAB, notably allowing Triple Axel to secure KOs on threats like Mega Latios and Raging Bolt after slight chip damage.

Balance and bulky offense teams appreciate its Meowscarada's ability to threaten common methods of speed control. Choice Scarf Meowscarada fits best on teams that appreciate its unmatched level of speed control, as it can handle faster Pokemon for its teammates, such as Tornadus-T and opposing Choice Scarf users like Landorus-T and Urshifu-R. Because of Meowscarada's ability to force switches and remove Heavy-Duty Boots, entry hazards are greatly appreciated; Pokemon that can set them up reliably include Ting-Lu, Iron Treads, and Gliscor. Their ability to set hazards up multiple times in a game works well with Meowscarada's Knock Off pressure, allowing for sustained chip damage. Because it tends to pivot with U-turn, Pokemon that remove entry hazards are also appreciated, such as Terapagos, Great Tusk, and Gliscor. In return, Meowscarada can use its Speed to revenge kill for its slower teammates, taking out threats to the aforementioned partner like Urshifu-R, Hisuian Samurott, and Ogerpon-W. Meowscarada is unable to break defensive Pokemon like Ferrothorn, Moltres, and Corviknight; thus, strong wallbreakers like Raging Bolt, Zamazenta, and Urshifu-R make for good partners. In return, Meowscarada can remove or threaten faster Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and boosted Dragonite, giving its teammates more opportunities to wallbreak. Because Meowscarada is commonly forced out by Fire- and Flying-type foes such as Moltres, Mega Charizard Y, and Corviknight, partners that can switch into them like Raging Bolt, Alomomola, and Gholdengo are appreciated. In return, Meowscarada can threaten the Ground- and Grass-type Pokemon that commonly target these teammates, such as Garchomp, Gliscor, and Rillaboom, using its Speed and the threat of Triple Axel to force them out.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf (Dark)
movesets.description: Thanks to its fantastic movepool and Protean, Choice Scarf Meowscarada is the best revenge killer available for Dark teams, outrunning the likes of Regieleki, Speed-boosted Kommo-o, and Mega Swampert under rain. Flower Trick is Meowscarada's most powerful move, picking off weakened foes such as Tapu Lele and Terrakion. Play Rough is essential, as it deals with many threats to Dark teams like Galarian Zapdos, Mega Gallade, and Iron Valiant. U-turn allows Meowscarada to switch out of unfavorable situations, pivoting into powerful teammates such as Galarian Moltres and Mega Tyranitar while keeping momentum for the team. Knock Off cripples defensive switch-ins—such as Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Clefable—as well as offensive Pokemon like Zeraora and Iron Treads. Toxic Spikes can be run instead to better pressure Normal, Fairy, and Fighting teams. Meowscarada's teammates appreciate its ability to check a myriad of threats as well as its revenge killing capabilities. Wallbreakers like Galarian Moltres and Hydreigon are great partners to deal with physical walls like Celesteela and Mega Venusaur. Ting-Lu and Tyranitar provide entry hazard support for Meowscarada—ensuring it is able to net more KO's—and are great defensive pivots for it to fall back upon. Similarly, Mega Sableye provides a Fighting immunity, bounces back status moves, and prevents entry hazards from going up, letting Meowscarada switch in unscathed.

movesets.name: Choice Scarf (Grass)
movesets.description: Meowscarada is an excellent choice for Grass teams thanks to its high Speed and Protean, enabling it to be a threatening revenge killer that can outspeed common threats such as Choice Scarf Iron Valiant and Gholdengo. Flower Trick is Meowscarada's best STAB option and is capable of dealing with weakened Pokemon like Clodsire and Spectrier. Flower Trick's guaranteed critical hit is also very useful in the Fairy matchup and lets Meowscarada revenge kill Azumarill and a weakened Tapu Lele behind Reflect. U-turn allows Meowscarada to maintain an advantage against its defensive checks like Corviknight by being able to pivot into its teammates like Scovillain. Knock Off is a tool to cripple Meowscarada's defensive switch-ins like Toxapex and Klefki in addition to the aforementioned Corviknight. Play Rough is a strong coverage option to threaten opposing Dragon-type Pokemon like Kommo-o, Kyurem, and Latios, which Grass teams tend to struggle against. Low Kick is a less frequent option but lets Meowscarada OHKO Bisharp while threatening Heatran with a 2HKO; however, Play Rough is preferred to have an easier time against Dragon teams. Meowscarada has an easier time revenge killing foes with entry hazard support from Ferrothorn and Cradily. Ferrothorn appreciates Meowscarada's ability to check Fighting-types like Mega Gallade, Iron Valiant and Galarian Zapdos with STAB Play Rough. Hisuian Lilligant is also a fantastic offensive partner for Meowscarada. It is able to check the Flying-types that switch into Meowscarada like Celesteela and Landorus-T while also assisting in the Dragon matchup, outspeeding common Pokemon like Garchomp and Dragonite. Hisuian Lilligant also makes the Steel matchup easier for Grass; its ability to threaten Heatran is appreciated by Meowscarada, while Meowscarada can threaten Gholdengo with Knock Off, which Lilligant cannot beat. Mega Venusaur is also a mandatory defensive partner for Meowscarada; its Bug neutrality and bulk allows it to act as a consistent check to Mega Scizor, which easily switches into any move of Meowscarada, and Venusaur is able to check it with Hidden Power Fire. Mega Venusaur also checks opposing Fairy-types for Meowscarada like Tapu Koko, Mega Diancie, and Iron Valiant, while Meowscarada is able to threaten the Psychic-types that force out Mega Venusaur such as Latios, Mega Alakazam, and Victini. Whismicott is one of the best hazard removal options on Grass, and Meowscarada appreciates not having Stealth Rock and Spikes chip it down, because it comes in often to threaten a KO. Whimsicott's Fairy typing also allows Meowscarada and its teammates not to be overwhelmed by Dragon-types like Garchomp, and it can encore Calm Mind Mega Latias. Celebi with Nasty Plot and Groundium Z can break defensive Steel-types like Heatran and Hisuian Goodra while also being able to threaten opposing Poison-types like Alolan Muk and Toxapex.
